SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.34
EXPLANATION: The strongest experimental Raman band is at 517 cm⁻¹.  Alkyl-bromide C–Br stretches lie in the 650–510 cm⁻¹ interval and are very Raman-active because of the highly-polarizable Br atom; 517 cm⁻¹ matches the low end of this range and would be expected to dominate the spectrum of a simple alkyl bromide.  
The spectrum also shows typical alkyl features:  

• Two intense C–H stretching peaks at 2929 and 2973 cm⁻¹ plus medium CH₃ deformation at 1458 cm⁻¹ are characteristic of a tert-butyl group.  
• CH₃ rocking / wagging modes of branched alkanes appear near 1140 cm⁻¹ (observed 1142 cm⁻¹) and C–C skeletal stretches in saturated chains appear near 800 cm⁻¹ (observed 805 cm⁻¹).  
• No strong bands are seen in regions expected for C=O (~1700 cm⁻¹), S=O (~1030–1080 cm⁻¹), C=S (~1200–1300 cm⁻¹) or other hetero-atom double bonds present in alternative candidates.  

Among the candidates only 1 (CC(C)(C)Br, tert-butyl bromide) contains a single C–Br bond with the simple saturated hydrocarbon skeleton matching all the observed alkyl vibrational features without introducing missing hetero-atom bands.
